notes.etonnya: Enjura neegwa, literally “the rain is falling”.
notes.gwaka: Omushana nigwaaka, the sun is shining.
notes.obudde: Obwire is the weather and also time.
notes.ttoggo: Itumba, the long rains around March to May.
notes.empewo: Obutiti, cold; nimpurira obutiti, I feel cold.

guidebook.intro: Talk about the weather and the seasons. Rain and sun “do things” in Runyankore: rain falls and the sun burns.

tips.title: The weather does things
body: **Enjura neegwa** is “it’s raining”, literally “the rain is falling”. **Omushana nigwaaka**, “the sun is burning”, means it’s sunny. **Nibwotsya** means it’s hot (the weather is burning).
To say how you feel, use **Nimpurira**: **Nimpurira obutiti** (I feel cold).

tips.title: Wet and dry
body: The long rains are **itumba**, and the rains later in the year are **omuhanga**. The dry season is **ekyanda**. **Obwire** means the weather and also time: **Obwire ni burungi** (the weather is nice).

culture.title: Planting with the rains
body: Farmers in Ankole plant millet, beans and bananas with the rains, and herders move cattle to find water and grass in the dry season.
